name: THE PENDELBURY
tagline: A country house hotel in the Cotswolds, est. 1887

brief.name: The Pendelbury
brief.industry: Independent country-house hotel & dining room in the Cotswolds — 18 rooms, a walled garden, an open fire, and a kitchen led by produce
brief.audience: UK and international guests 35-70 seeking understated heritage luxury for anniversaries, long weekends, and country weddings; readers of Country Life and The Gentlewoman.
brief.tone: understated, assured, established, warm, literate, never loud
brief.references: Fortnum & Mason, The Newt in Somerset, Country Life, Penguin Classics typography, Wimbledon's restraint
brief.context: Hero with the house set in a classic English serif (Caslon/Baskerville), 'est. 1887'. Sections: the house & its history, the rooms (with seasonal rates in £), the dining room, the garden & grounds, and a 'Book your stay / By arrangement' enquiry. Racing-green / oxblood / brass on cream. Fine hairline rules and an engraved feel.
brief.avoid: Silicon-Valley sans (Inter/Helvetica) as the voice. Union-Jack bunting or 'keep calm' parody. Neon or gradients. Exclamation-mark marketing. Stocky 'luxury hotel' clichés that read as a chain.
